question.problem:
If $A=\{-2,2\}$ and $B=\{c,d\},$ which of the following elements belong to $(A\times B)\times B?$

I. $(-2,d,c)$

II. $(-2,(c,d))$

III. $((2,d),c)$
question.worked_solution:
The Cartesian product $A\times B$ consists of all ordered pairs whose first coordinate belongs to $A$ and whose second coordinate belongs to $B.$

In this case, $A\times B$ consists of every combination of ${-2,2}$ with ${c,d},$ as shown in the schematic below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14123139/assets/98e7cfca515290b952ea5aefc9b2516a5cd6a68de0dc048c2075128e6c60b651.png)

Hence, the set $A\times B$ is given by

$$
A\times B={(-2,c),(-2,d),(2,c),(2,d)}.
$$

Note that 

$$
|A\times B|=|A|\cdot |B|=2\cdot 2=4.
$$

Now, the Cartesian product

$$
(A\times B)\times B
$$

consists of every combination of $A\times B$ and $B,$ as shown in the schematic below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14123139/assets/1e96aeb1c5bfb1f9faa590a8eb8b01528a1ce9431a3f1ceac92b156a9bdde221.png)

Note that 

$$
|(A\times B)\times B|=|A\times B|\cdot |B|=4\cdot 2=8.
$$

From the given options, we see that only $((2,d),c)\in (A\times B)\times B.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."
